photon.gui.editor.timeline.time.tip: Current time (seconds); type a value and click away to jump
photon.gui.editor.timeline.end_mode.tip: End condition: wait until every FX object is finished (off), or stop at the timeline's end (on)
photon.gui.editor.timeline.wrap_mode.tip: On end: restart from the beginning / loop (on), or hold at the last frame (off)
photon.gui.editor.timeline.mute: Mute track — its clips stop evaluating while muted (animations stop applying, post-process clips stop submitting, signals/audio don't fire)
photon.gui.editor.timeline.lock: Lock track — its clips can't be selected, moved or edited until unlocked
photon.gui.editor.timeline.property.expr: §et§r denotes the time in ticks since the clip start
kg.node.photon_fullscreen_position.toolt: The fixed fullscreen vertex transform: the pass draws a screen-covering quad, so the clip-space position is the quad corner itself. Required — do not delete.
The vertex half of every post pass. The executor draws a quad whose POSITION attribute is already in clip space (±1), so this block passes it straight through — no model, view or projection matrix is involved.
Created by the default graph and non-deletable: without it the compiler falls back to the ProjMat · ModelViewMat path, and a fullscreen dispatch has no matrices bound.
kg.node.photon_fullscreen_output.tooltip: The pass's final color (rgb) and alpha (default 1). A post pass writes exactly one output color.
kg.node.photon_fullscreen_output.desc.1: The fragment half of every post pass, and its only output. Color (vec3) is what lands in the pass's render target; Alpha (float, default 1) is its coverage — post targets are opaque unless the effect deliberately writes alpha.
kg.node.photon_fullscreen_output.desc.2: The particle pipeline's separate Base Color / Alpha / Emission / Discard blocks have no meaning here: a fullscreen pass writes exactly one fragColor.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.tooltip: The size of a bound texture: size = (width, height) pixels, texelSize = (1/width, 1/height) — the primitive blur/downsample kernels need. Only samplers bound by the effect executor carry a size; plain asset textures read 0.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.desc.1: The resolution of a bound texture — the primitive every blur, downsample and edge kernel needs to step by exactly one pixel.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.desc.2: Backed by a per-sampler <name>_TexelSize uniform (w, h, 1/w, 1/h) that the effect executor sets for every render-target input it binds, so the same graph is correct at every size a pass is dispatched at.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.in.sampler: The texture to measure — wire the same sampler you are going to sample.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.out.texelSize: (1/width, 1/height) — one texel step in UV space.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.example.1: uv + texelSize * offset samples the neighbouring pixel whatever the target resolution is, so one blur graph serves every mip of a bloom pyramid.
kg.node.photon_texel_size.note.1: Samplers the executor does not bind (plain asset textures) have no size uniform and read 0 — feed those through a constant instead.
kg.node.photon_scene_color_input.tooltip: The effect chain's input color — the scene as rendered so far, in HDR.
kg.node.photon_scene_color_input.desc.1: What the effect starts from: the scene color at this point on the effect axis, with every lower-priority effect already applied. Wire it into the pass inputs that should see the scene.
kg.node.photon_scene_color_input.note.1: HDR (RGBA16F) — values above 1 are real. Don't assume 0..1 when thresholding or tone-mapping.
kg.node.photon_scene_depth_input.tooltip: The scene depth texture (raw hardware depth — sample .r in the fullscreen graph).
kg.node.photon_scene_depth_input.desc.1: The depth buffer that goes with Scene Color — the input for depth-aware effects (fog, depth of field, edge detection, world-space reconstruction).
kg.node.photon_scene_depth_input.out.out: The depth texture; the depth value is in the red channel.
kg.node.photon_scene_depth_input.note.1: Raw hardware depth, which is non-linear: linearize it before doing distance math.
kg.node.photon_custom_mask_input.tooltip: The custom mask texture: R = mask id / 255 of the FX passes that enabled Write Custom Mask, 0 elsewhere. Empty (black) on frames where nothing is flagged. Match a group in a shader via round(R * 255).
kg.node.photon_custom_mask_input.desc.1: Unreal's CustomStencil, Photon-style: which pixels the flagged FX cover. Only emitters whose renderer enabled Write Custom Mask draw into it, so an effect can be confined to your own particles.
kg.node.photon_custom_mask_input.out.out: The mask texture: R = group id / 255, 0 where nothing was flagged.
kg.node.photon_custom_mask_input.example: round(R * 255) recovers the group id — compare it against one group to isolate a single emitter's pixels.
kg.node.photon_custom_mask_input.note.1: Black on frames where nothing is flagged. The timeline clip's Mask Filter already culls a whole effect by group; use this node when the graph itself needs the mask.
kg.node.photon_custom_depth_input.toolti: The custom depth texture: the mask target's own depth — pre-filled with the scene depth, then overwritten only by the FX passes that enabled Write Custom Mask.
kg.node.photon_custom_depth_input.desc.1: Unreal's CustomDepth: how far away the flagged FX are, over a pre-fill of the scene depth. Pairs with Custom Mask when an effect needs the depth of the particles it isolates, not the depth of the world behind them.
kg.node.photon_custom_depth_input.out.ou: The custom depth texture (raw hardware depth).
kg.node.photon_custom_depth_input.exampl: Compare it with Scene Depth to tell flagged FX in front of geometry from FX hidden behind it — occlusion-aware outlines and glows.
kg.node.photon_effect_weight.tooltip: The effect's blended request weight (0..1) — driven by timeline clip fades and the submit API. Wire it into a pass float parameter to react to fades physically (e.g. scale a distortion amount); usually the automatic final mix already handles fading and you don't need this.
kg.node.photon_effect_weight.desc.1: This frame's blended request weight for the whole effect, as a wireable float: 1 while fully requested, fading with timeline clip fades and the submit API.
kg.node.photon_effect_weight.desc.2: Wire it into any pass parameter to make a fade change what the effect does — shrink a blur radius, scale a distortion — instead of only cross-fading the finished image.
kg.node.photon_effect_weight.note.1: Effect Output's Auto Blend already fades the effect by weight, so most graphs never need this node. Passes that don't wire it are unaffected.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.tooltip: Feeds an external texture into a pass: either an image baked into the effect, or a named sampler parameter set per timeline clip.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.desc.1: The effect graph's counterpart of the fullscreen graph's Texture node — everything a pass samples that isn't a scene input or another pass's output comes from here (noise, gradients, LUTs, masks).
kg.node.photon_texture_input.out.out: The texture; wire it into any pass's texture input.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.option.mode: A fixed image baked into the effect.
A named sampler parameter, exposed in the timeline clip inspector and set per clip.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.option.text: The texture: the baked image in ASSET mode, or the parameter's default in PARAMETER mode.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.option.name: The sampler parameter's name (PARAMETER mode) — the label shown in the clip inspector.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.note.1: Samplers can't be blackboard variables, so this node is the only way to expose one as an effect parameter.
kg.node.photon_texture_input.note.2: Samplers don't interpolate: overlapping clips of the same effect take the highest-weight one rather than blending.
kg.node.photon_pass.tooltip: One fullscreen dispatch: runs a fullscreen shader graph over its inputs into its own render target.
kg.node.photon_pass.desc.1: The workhorse of an effect graph. A pass mirrors its source's interface as ports: every SAMPLER2D input becomes a texture port (wire a scene input or another pass's output), every exposed uniform becomes a typed value port you can set inline or wire from a blackboard parameter.
kg.node.photon_pass.desc.2: Its single output is the pass's own render target, sized by the Size option. Chaining passes is how effects are built — an INPUT_RELATIVE ×0.5 chain is a manually unrolled downsample pyramid.
kg.node.photon_pass.option.source.toolti: The fullscreen shader graph this pass dispatches. Its SAMPLER2D inputs become texture ports; its exposed uniforms become value ports.
kg.node.photon_pass.option.size.tooltip: Output target sizing: SCREEN_RELATIVE = screen × scale; INPUT_RELATIVE = a texture input's resolved size × scale (×0.5 chains build downsample pyramids); ABSOLUTE = fixed pixels. INPUT_RELATIVE derives from the named texture input, or the first one when left blank.
kg.node.photon_pass.option.format.toolti: The output target's pixel format. RGBA16F (HDR) unless you know you need less.
8-bit color — LDR only, but a quarter of the bandwidth.
Two float channels, e.g. packed velocity or a two-channel blur.
One float channel — masks and luminance that need range.
One byte channel — what the CustomMask target itself uses.
kg.node.photon_pass.note.1: Ports are keyed by the source's variable display name: renaming a variable in the fullscreen graph orphans the wires on existing pass nodes — reconnect them.
kg.node.photon_pass.note.2: The Weight variable is engine-driven and never becomes a port; use the Effect Weight node when a pass needs it wired.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.tooltip: The effect's fixed output: whatever texture feeds Color becomes the new scene color. Also carries the effect-level settings.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.desc.1: Where the effect chain ends: the texture wired into Color replaces the scene color for everything that runs after this effect.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.in.color: The texture that becomes the new scene color.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.option.prio: Execution order on the global effect axis: builtin bloom = 0, lower runs before it, higher after. Ties break by effect path.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.option.auto: Automatically mix(scene, effect, Weight) so the effect fades with request weight / timeline clip fades. Disable if the graph handles Weight itself.
kg.node.photon_effect_output.note.1: Created by the graph and non-deletable — an effect has exactly one output.
photon.render_graph.preview.no_frame: No world frame captured — open the editor in-game with a world rendering behind it.
photon.render_graph.dive.read_only: This fullscreen graph is read-only (builtin/pack) — you can inspect it, but saves are rejected. Copy it into the project to edit.
The post-processing effect (Effect Graph asset) this clip requests every frame while active. Stop of the clip = stop of the effect; overlapping clips of the same effect blend by weight.

Request weight 0..1 sampled at the clip's progress (t=0 start, t=1 end) — a curve here IS the fade envelope. It drives the automatic scene/effect mix and the parameter blending between overlapping clips.

CustomMask culling for this clip: toggle on to apply the effect only where flagged FX wrote masks (works with EVERY effect - the final mix becomes mix(scene, effect, weight * mask match)). Off = fullscreen.
The mask group NAME to target (the emitter renderer Mask Group). Leave empty to apply wherever ANY group is set. Several clips of the same effect targeting different groups cull their exact union.

Run this clip as its OWN fullscreen execution instead of merging with other requests of the same effect - keeps this clip's parameters, weight and mask filter fully separate (e.g. two outline clips with different colors on different mask groups). Costs one extra execution while active.

The effect's blackboard parameters. Rows show the effect defaults; any edit turns the row into a clip override (orange) sampled over the clip — INT rounds, BOOL is sample ≥ 0.5, colors sample gradients, vectors sample one function per channel.
photon.is_mask_visible: Show the CustomMask contents instead of the scene (the builtin show_mask debug view; groups are hue-colored). Default off.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.tooltip: The particle's per-vertex data (works on CPU quads, trails, beams and both GPU-instanced modes): position (camera-relative world), raw color, lightmap-lit color, UV and normal (world). A Position/Normal node's 'Object' space is meaningful on the instanced paths (model instancing = mesh-local; billboards = centered quad coord) and degenerates to World on the CPU/trail/beam paths.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.desc.1: Everything Photon hands the shader per vertex. All five outputs come from the same read, and that read works on every path — CPU quads, trails, beams and both GPU-instanced modes — so a graph built on this node keeps working whatever the emitter renders as.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.desc.2: Interpolated into the fragment stage, so the outputs are usable in both stages.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.out.positio: The vertex position relative to the camera (1.21 renders camera-relative). Add the camera position back for absolute world coordinates.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.out.color: The particle's own color, before lighting.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.out.litColo: Color × the baked lightmap — how a vanilla particle ends up lit. Use it when the effect should respect block and sky light.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.out.uv: Texture coordinates: the sprite frame UV for particles, the length UV for trails and beams.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.out.normal: The surface normal, in world space.
kg.node.photon_particle_data.note.1: A Position or Normal node's Object space is only meaningful on the instanced paths (model instancing = mesh-local, billboards = the centered quad coordinate); on the CPU, trail and beam paths it degenerates to World.
kg.node.photon_additional_data.tooltip: Reads one per-instance Additional GPU Data channel (T, velocity, per-point trail data, beam direction...). Requires GPU instancing on the emitter — the channel is auto-enabled for you. Reads 0 on the CPU path, in previews, and on particle kinds that don't support the channel.
kg.node.photon_additional_data.desc.1: Reads one channel of the emitter's per-instance Additional GPU Data — normalized lifetime T, velocity, per-point trail data, beam direction and the rest of the registry listed below.
kg.node.photon_additional_data.desc.2: The read happens in the vertex stage and is routed through a varying for you, so the value is usable in both stages. The output type follows the channel (float or vec3).
kg.node.photon_additional_data.out.out: The channel's value for this particle.
kg.node.photon_additional_data.option.ch: The data channel to read. Its type follows the channel (float or vec3).
kg.node.photon_additional_data.note.1: Requires GPU instancing on the emitter, but not a trip to the Additional Data settings: the channels a graph reads are enabled automatically.
kg.node.photon_additional_data.note.2: Reads 0 on the CPU (non-instanced) path, in node previews, and on particle kinds that don't carry the channel (e.g. a trail channel on a billboard).
kg.node.photon_custom_data.tooltip: Reads one user Custom Data stream (defined per-emitter in Additional Data) by its index and outputs it as a vec4 — always a vec4 regardless of how many channels the stream defines (unused channels read 0). Requires GPU instancing; the stream is uploaded for you. Reads vec4(0) on the CPU path, in previews, and for indices the emitter doesn't define.
kg.node.photon_custom_data.desc.1: Reads one of the emitter's user Custom Data streams (Unity-style, authored per emitter under Additional Data) by index — the way to drive a shader from curves and gradients the artist edits on the emitter.
kg.node.photon_custom_data.desc.2: The output is always a vec4 no matter how many channels the stream defines (unused channels read 0); swizzle out the ones you need. Like Additional Data, the read is routed through a varying and works in both stages.
kg.node.photon_custom_data.out.out: The stream's four channels for this particle.
Which Custom Data stream to read (0-based). Out-of-range indices read vec4(0).
kg.node.photon_custom_data.note.1: Requires GPU instancing; the stream buffer is uploaded automatically when a graph reads it.
kg.node.photon_custom_data.note.2: Reads vec4(0) on the CPU path, in node previews, and for indices the emitter doesn't define (an emitter has at most 4 streams).
photon.custom_data.tips: User-defined per-particle data streams (Unity-style Custom Data), each uploaded as a vec4. Read them in a hand-written shader as vec4 attributes appended after the enabled channels above, or in a shader graph via the Custom Data node. Only the first 4 streams are used.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.tooltip: Soft particles: 0 where the fragment touches opaque geometry, 1 once it is Distance blocks in front. Multiply into alpha to hide hard intersections. Translucent materials only; previews show 1.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.desc.1: Soft particles, Unreal's DepthFade: 0 where this fragment touches the opaque geometry behind it, rising to 1 once it is Distance blocks in front of it.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.desc.2: Multiply it into alpha and the hard line where a particle clips the ground or a wall dissolves into a soft edge.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.in.distance: The fade distance in blocks — how far in front of geometry the particle becomes fully opaque. Larger fades over a longer distance.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.example.1: Depth Fade into Multiply with the particle alpha is the whole soft-particle recipe; a Distance of 0.5-1 suits smoke and dust.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.note.1: Fragment-only, and it reads the pipeline's scene depth capture — translucent materials only.
kg.node.photon_depth_fade.note.2: Node previews show a constant 1: there is no scene behind the preview to fade against.
kg.node.photon_viewport.tooltip: The active viewport: this fragment's 0-1 screen UV and the viewport size in pixels.
kg.node.photon_viewport.desc.1: The viewport being drawn into (x, y, width, height — bound from the GL viewport each draw), as the two values a shader actually wants from it.
kg.node.photon_viewport.out.screenUv: This fragment's 0..1 position on screen — the UV Scene Color and Scene Depth sample with.
kg.node.photon_viewport.out.size: The viewport size in pixels, for pixel-perfect effects and aspect correction.
kg.node.photon_viewport.note.1: Fragment-only: it reads gl_FragCoord. Use World To Screen UV when the vertex stage needs a screen UV.
kg.node.photon_viewport.note.2: In node previews screenUv falls back to the mesh UV.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.toolti: Projects a Position to a window-relative screen UV (feed Scene Color / Scene Depth). Works in vertex and fragment. Space: Absolute = world coordinates (camera position subtracted for you); Camera-Relative = already camera-relative, e.g. ParticleData.Position.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.desc.1: Projects any position into the same window-relative screen UV that Scene Color and Scene Depth sample in — where on screen a point in the world lands.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.desc.2: Pure uniform math, no gl_FragCoord, so unlike the Viewport node it works in the vertex stage as well as the fragment stage.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.in.pos: The point to project, in the space chosen by the Space option.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.out.uv: The window-relative screen UV of that point.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.option: Position is absolute world/block coordinates; the camera position is subtracted for you.
Position is already relative to the camera (e.g. ParticleData.Position); projected directly.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.exampl: ParticleData.Position (Camera-Relative) into this node, then into Scene Color, samples whatever the particle is drawn over — the basis of refraction and heat haze.
kg.node.photon_world_to_screen_uv.note.1: The projection is remapped through the viewport into the window-sized scene capture, so it is correct in-world and inside the editor's sub-viewport scene alike.
photon.shader_graph.graph.tip: The shader graph asset this material renders with. Its exposed variables appear below as per-material values.
photon.shader_graph.variables.tip: The graph's exposed variables. Rows show the graph defaults; editing stores a per-material override (orange title) — the REPLAY square resets it back to the graph default.
photon.resource.no_file_provider.title: No File Provider
photon.resource.no_file_provider.info: Add a file resource provider in the resource panel first.
photon.fx_object.name: Name
photon.emitter.config.duration: The duration of time (tick) the Emitter. If the system is looping, this indicates the length of one cycle.
photon.emitter.config.looping: If true, the emission cycle will repeat after the duration.
photon.emitter.config.startDelay: Delay in ticks that this Particle System will wait before emitting particles.
photon.emitter.config.startLifetime: Start lifetime in ticks, particle will die when its lifetime reaches 0.
photon.emitter.config.startSpeed: The start speed of particles, applied in the starting direction.
photon.emitter.config.startRotation: The start rotation of particles in degrees. (x-roll, y-pitch, z-yaw)
photon.emitter.config.simulationSpace: Controls whether particles are animated in the parent object’s local space (therefore moving with the parent object).
photon.emitter.config.maxParticles: The number of particles in the system will be limited by this number. Emission will be temporarily halted if this is reached.
photon.emitter.config.parallelUpdate.0: Should particles be updated in parallel threads. It will improve performance when you have massive particles. e.g., use it can improve noise calculation performance.
photon.emitter.config.parallelUpdate.1: §cThis does not always improve performance and sometimes degrade performance§r
photon.emitter.config.emission: Emission of the emitter. This controls the rate at which particles are emitted as well as burst emissions.
photon.emitter.config.shape: Shape of the emitter volume, which controls where particles are emitted and their initial direction.
photon.emitter.config.renderer: Specifies how the particles are rendered.
photon.emitter.config.lights: Controls the light map of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.velocityOverLifeti: Controls the velocity of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.inheritVelocity: Controls the velocity inherited from the emitter, foreach particle.
photon.emitter.config.lifetimeByEmitterS: Controls the initial lifetime of each particle based on the speed of the emitter when the particle was spawned.
photon.emitter.config.forceOverLifetime: Controls the force of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.colorOverLifetime: Controls the color of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.colorBySpeed: Controls the color of each particle based on its speed.
photon.emitter.config.sizeOverLifetime: Controls the size of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.sizeBySpeed: Controls the size of each particle based on its speed.
photon.emitter.config.rotationOverLifeti: Controls the rotation of each particle during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.rotationBySpeed: Controls the angular velocity of each particle based on its speed.
photon.emitter.config.noise: Add noise/turbulence to particle movement. If you have many particles, you should also check parallelUpdate for better performance.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation: Particle UV animation. This allows you to specify a texture sheet (a texture with multiple tiles/subframes) and animate or randomize over it per particle.
photon.emitter.config.colorBySpeed.color: Controls the color by its speed.
photon.emitter.config.colorBySpeed.speed: Remaps speed in the defined range to a color.
Controls the color during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.emission.emissionR: The number of particles emitted per tick. The decimal part calculates the probability.
photon.emitter.config.emission.distanceR: The rate of particles emitted per meter. The decimal part calculates the probability.
photon.emitter.config.emission.emissionM: The emission mode of the decimal part, fixed interval emission or random emission.
photon.emitter.config.emission.bursts: Emission of extra particles at specific times during the duration of the system.
photon.emitter.config.emission.bursts.co: The number of particles to emit.
photon.emitter.config.emission.bursts.cy: How many times to emit the burst. (0 - repeat infinitely)
photon.emitter.config.emission.bursts.in: Repeat the burst every N ticks.
photon.emitter.config.emission.bursts.pr: 0-1 Chance that the burst will trigger.
photon.emitter.config.inheritVelocity.mo: Specifies whether the emitter velocity is inherited as a one-shot when a particle is born, always using the current emitter velocity, or using the emitter velocity when the particle was born.
photon.emitter.config.inheritVelocity.mu: Controls the amount of emitter velocity inherited during each particle's lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.lifetimeByEmitterS: Controls the initial lifetime of particles based on the speed of the emitter.
Maps the speed to a value along the curve, when using one of the curve modes.
photon.emitter.config.lights.skyLight: Sky Light value for lighting map. (0-15)
photon.emitter.config.lights.blockLight: Block Light value for lighting map. (0-15)
photon.emitter.config.noise.frequency: Low values create soft, smooth noise, and high values create rapidly changing noise.
photon.emitter.config.noise.remap: Remap the final noise values into a new range.
photon.emitter.config.noise.position: How strong the overall noise effect is. If you use a curve to set this value, the Particle System applies the curve over the lifetime of each particle.
photon.emitter.config.noise.rotation: What proportion of the noise is applied to the particle rotations,in degrees per second. If you use a curve to set this value, the Particle System applies the curve over the lifetime of each particle.
photon.emitter.config.noise.size: Multiply the size of the particle by a proportion of the noise.If you use a curve to set this value, theParticle System applies the curve over the life time of each particle.
photon.emitter.config.physics.removedWhe: Remove the particle when the collision happens.
photon.emitter.config.physics.friction: The friction of particles over lifetime. (0-infinite friction, 1-frictionless)
photon.emitter.config.physics.gravity: The gravity of particles over lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.physics.bounceChan: The possibility of bounce when it has physics.
photon.emitter.config.physics.bounceRate: The bounce rate of speed when collision happens.
photon.emitter.config.physics.bounceSpre: Addition velocity for other two axis gaussian noise when collision happens.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.renderMod: Defines the render mode of the particle renderer.
If enabled, the model will be rendered with shade for each side
If enabled, use uv according to the model, otherwise use the particle uv.
Stretches particles proportionally to their current size along the direction of their velocity. Setting this to zero makes the particles disappear, having effectively zero length.
Stretches particles proportionally to their speed. Set this to zero to disable stretching based on speed.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.facingMod: Defines the facing algorithm used by Billboard render mode.
default: keep Photon's original Billboard behavior and use the camera rotation directly.
rotate_y: aligned to the camera, but rotating around world Y axis.
lookat_xyz: aimed at the camera, biased towards world Y up.
lookat_y: aimed at the camera, but rotating around world Y axis.
lookat_direction: use the direction input to orient the particle while it continues to face the camera.
direction_x: unrotated particle X axis is along the direction vector, and unrotated Y axis attempts to aim upwards.
direction_y: unrotated particle Y axis is along the direction vector, and unrotated X axis attempts to aim upwards.
direction_z: billboard face is along the direction vector, and unrotated particle Y axis attempts to aim upwards.
emitter_transform_xy: orient the particles to match the emitter transform; the billboard plane will match the emitter's XY plane.
emitter_transform_xz: orient the particles to match the emitter transform; the billboard plane will match the emitter's XZ plane.
emitter_transform_yz: orient the particles to match the emitter transform; the billboard plane will match the emitter's YZ plane.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.facingDir: Choose whether the facing direction comes from particle velocity or a custom local direction.
Minimum particle speed required before velocity-derived facing is used.
Custom local direction used for Billboard facing. It will be transformed by the particle space rotation.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.layer: Defines the render layer of the particle renderer.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.bloomEffe: Render particles with the bloom effect.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.cull: Cull particles that are out of view.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.orderInLa: Emitter's layer within a sorted layer
photon.emitter.config.renderer.writeCust: Redraw this emitter into the custom mask target (Unreal CustomDepth/Stencil-style): post effects can then target it through the Custom Mask / Custom Depth input nodes - e.g. the builtin mask_outline effect. Zero cost while nothing is flagged.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.maskGroup: The named mask group this emitter writes (any string, e.g. boss / fire_aura). Effects and clips target groups by the same name; ids are assigned automatically behind the scenes.
photon.emitter.config.renderer.maskAlpha: 0 = off: the mask covers the whole geometry (a rectangle for billboards). Above 0 the mask sub-pass samples the pass texture and discards fragments below the cutoff, clipping the mask to the sprite shape (needs a texture material on the pass).
photon.emitter.config.renderer.vertexSor: Whether sorting the vertex before rendering. Useful for translucent quad
photon.emitter.config.rotationBySpeed.sp: Remaps speed in the defined range to a rotation.
photon.emitter.config.sizeBySpeed.scale: Controls the scale of size by speed.
photon.emitter.config.sizeBySpeed.size: Controls the size of separated axis by speed.
photon.emitter.config.sizeBySpeed.speedR: Remaps speed in the defined range to a size.
photon.emitter.config.sizeOverLifetime.s: Controls the scale of size during its lifetime.
Controls the size of separated axis during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.trails.ratio: Choose what proportion of particles will receive a trail.
photon.emitter.config.trails.lifetime: How long each trail will last, relative to the life of the particle.
photon.emitter.config.trails.minimumVert: The minimum distance each trail can travel before adding a new vertex.
photon.emitter.config.trails.dieWithPart: The trails will disappear when their owning particles die.
photon.emitter.config.trails.uvMode: Should the U coordinate be stretched or tiled?
photon.emitter.config.trails.sizeAffects: The trails will use the particle size to control their width.
The trails will use the particle size to control their lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.trails.inheritPart: The trails will use the particle color as their base color.
photon.emitter.config.trails.colorOverLi: The color of the trails during the lifetime of the particle they are attached to.
photon.emitter.config.trails.widthOverTr: Select a width for the trail from its start to end vertex.
photon.emitter.config.trails.colorOverTr: Select a color for the trail from its start to end vertex.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation.tiles: Defines the tiling of the texture.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation.animat: Specifies the animation type: Whole Sheet or SingleRow.Whole Sheet will animate over the whole texture sheet from left to right, top to bottom. SingleRow will animate a single row in the sheet from left to right.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation.frameO: Controls the uv animation frame of each particle over its lifetime. On the horizontal axis you will find the lifetime.On the vertical axis you will find the sheet index.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation.startF: Phase the animation, so it starts on a frame other than 0.
photon.emitter.config.uvAnimation.cycle: Specifies how many times the animation will loop during the lifetime of the particle.
photon.emitter.config.velocityOverLifeti: Which axes the values below are authored in. Local: the emitter's own axes, so rotating the effect re-aims them. World: absolute world axes. Independent of the emitter's simulation space.
Apply orbital velocity to particles, which will rotate them around the center of the system.
Apply an offset to the center of rotation.
Multiply the particle speed by this value.
photon.emitter.config.shape.mesh.type: Generate particles from vertices, edges or triangles.
photon.emitter.config.material.preview: Replace the material by dragging it into the preview.
photon.emitter.trail.config.time: How long the tail should be (ticks)[O, infinity].
photon.emitter.trail.config.minVertexDis: The minimum distance each trail can travel before adding a new vertex.
photon.emitter.trail.config.smoothInterp: Apply smooth interpolation to the trail.
If you enable it, increase the minVertexDistance as much as possible (We recommend greater than 0.1).
photon.emitter.trail.config.calculateSmo: If you enable it, the smooth trail will be calculated by the compute shader. Enable it when you have a massive number of tails to be smooth.

photon.emitter.trail.config.widthOverTra: Select a width for the trail from its start to end vertex.
photon.emitter.trail.config.colorOverTra: Select a color for the trail from its start to end vertex.
photon.emitter.config.sub_emitters: Sub emission of particles. This allows each particle to emit particles in another system.
photon.emitter.config.sub_emitters.emitt: Drag/Select an emitter here (using emitter name).

photon.emitter.config.additional_gpu_dat: To use it, you have to enable gpu instance, which allows to send particle's data to shader.
photon.emitter.beam.config.width: Controls the width during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.beam.config.emitRate: Controls the emit rate during its lifetime.
photon.emitter.beam.config.raycast: whether the beam's length will be reduced upon hitting an object
photon.emitter.beam.config.raycast.block: Affect how the raycast interacts with blocks.
photon.emitter.beam.config.raycast.fluid: Affect how the raycast interacts with fluids.
photon.emitter.beam.config.color: Controls the color during its lifetime.

addition_gpu_data.point_t.tips: Normalized position of the point along the trail: 0 - oldest tail, 1 - head.
addition_gpu_data.point_life.tips: Normalized age of the trail point: 0 - fresh, 1 - about to expire.
addition_gpu_data.beam_direction.tips: The beam's start-to-end vector (derived in the shader, nothing uploaded).
addition_gpu_data.beam_length.tips: The beam's length in blocks (derived in the shader, nothing uploaded).
photon.model_source.obj_model.flipV.tips: Mirror UVs vertically (v = 1 - v). OBJ files use a bottom-left UV origin, so most exports need this enabled.
photon.emitter.config.shape.arc: Arc module: controls how particles are sampled along the arc.
photon.emitter.config.shape.arc.mode: Mode: choose the arc sampling mode. Random samples randomly, Loop advances by emitter time, PingPong moves back and forth, BurstSpread distributes evenly within the same batch.
photon.emitter.config.shape.arc.spread: Spread: snaps the sampled value to fixed steps; 0 means no snapping, 1 snaps everything to the start. It only changes discrete stepping, not continuity.
photon.emitter.config.shape.arc.speed: Speed: used only by Loop and PingPong. In the current implementation, angle = emitterAge / 20 * speed, then mapped into the arc range.
photon.emitter.config.customSpace.tips: Custom space to simulate particles in (particles move with the referenced transform)
AraTrails.space.tips: Whether to use world or local space to generate and simulate the trail.
AraTrails.customSpace.tips: Custom space to use when generating and simulating the trail
AraTrails.alignment.tips: How to align the trail geometry: facing the camera (view) of using the transform's rotation (local).
AraTrails.sorting.tips: Determines the order in which trail points will be rendered.
AraTrails.smoothness.tips: Amount of smoothing iterations applied to the trail shape.
AraTrails.highQualityCorners.tips: Calculate accurate thickness at sharp corners.
AraTrails.thicknessOverLength.tips: How should the thickness of the curve evolve over its lenght. The horizontal axis is normalized lenght (in the [0,1] range) and the vertical axis is a thickness multiplier.
AraTrails.colorOverLength.tips: How should vertex color evolve over the trail's length.
AraTrails.thicknessOverTime.tips: How should the thickness of the curve evolve with its life(normalized emitter life). The horizontal axis is normalized lifetime (in the [0,1] range) and the vertical axis is a thickness multiplier.
AraTrails.thicknessOverSegmentTime.tips: How should the thickness of the curve evolve with the lifetime of its segments. The horizontal axis is normalized lifetime (in the [0,1] range) and the vertical axis is a thickness multiplier.
AraTrails.colorOverTime.tips: How should vertex color evolve over the trail's life(normalized emitter life).
AraTrails.colorOverSegmentTime.tips: How should vertex color evolve over the lifetime of segments.
AraTrails.initialThickness.tips: Initial thickness of trail points when they are first spawned.
AraTrails.initialColor.tips: Initial color of trail points when they are first spawned.
AraTrails.initialVelocity.tips: Initial velocity of trail points when they are first spawned.
AraTrails.minSpawnTime.tips: Minimum amount of time (in seconds) that must pass before spawning a new point.
AraTrails.minDistance.tips: Minimum distance (in meters) that must be left between consecutive points in the trail.
AraTrails.warmup.tips: Amount of seconds pre-simulated before the trail appears. Useful when you want a trail to be already simulating when the game starts.
AraTrails.inertia.tips: Amount of speed transferred from the transform to the trail. 0 means no velocity is transferred, 1 means 100% of the velocity is transferred.
AraTrails.velocitySmoothing.tips: Amount of temporal smoothing applied to the velocity transferred from the transform to the trail.
AraTrails.damping.tips: Amount of damping applied to the trail's velocity. Larger values will slow down the trail more as time passes.
AraTrails.textureMode.tips: How to apply the texture over the trail: stretch it all over its lenght, or tile it.
AraTrails.uvFactor.tips: Defines how many times are U coords repeated across the length of the trail.
AraTrails.uvWidthFactor.tips: Defines how many times are V coords repeated trough the width of the trail.
AraTrails.tileAnchor.tips: When the texture mode is set to 'Tile', defines where to begin tiling from: 0 means the start of the trail, 1 means the end.
AraTrails.section.tips: Trail cross-section asset, determines the shape of the emitted trail. If it is disabled, the trail will be a simple strip.
photon.emitter.config.prewarm: Amount of ticks pre-simulated before the first frame of rendering.
photon.emitter.config.velocityOverLifeti: Radial velocity of particles away from/towards the center position.
photon.emitter.config.externalForces: Lets force fields in the same FX affect this emitter's particles.
photon.emitter.config.externalForces.mul: Scales the strength of all force fields affecting this emitter, over the particle's lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.externalForces.inf: SceneAll: every force field in this FX affects the emitter. List: only the referenced force fields do.
The force fields that affect this emitter (drag force field nodes from the hierarchy).
photon.force_field.shape: The shape of the field's influence volume.
photon.force_field.startRange: Influence is at full strength inside this range and falls off linearly towards the end range.
photon.force_field.endRange: The outer extent of the field's influence volume.
photon.force_field.direction: Directional force applied along the field's local axes, over the particle's lifetime.
photon.force_field.gravity: Strength of the attraction towards the gravity focus point, over the particle's lifetime.
photon.force_field.gravityFocus: Where particles are pulled to: 0 = the field's center, 1 = the edge of the influence volume.
photon.force_field.rotationSpeed: Speed of the vortex rotation around the field's local Y axis, over the particle's lifetime.
photon.force_field.rotationAttraction: How strongly particles are dragged into the vortex motion (0 = no attraction, 1 = full).
photon.force_field.rotationRandomness: Randomly offsets the vortex axis per particle along the field's local X/Z axes.
photon.force_field.drag: Slows particles down inside the influence volume, over the particle's lifetime.
photon.emitter.config.physics.collidedFr: Friction applied when particles is collided
